metadata.note: HAND-AUTHORED AND HAND-VERIFIED. The builder reads this and never writes it, so a regeneration cannot overwrite a judgement made here. Rows were proposed by scripts/mailchimp/propose-crosswalk.ts and every one was read before landing. 55 of the 64 were settled through the Humanitix crosswalk rather than by title similarity: the Event: tags were pasted into Mailchimp from Humanitix ticket lists, so they carry Humanitix listing names, and those names were already tied to site events by date and registration count. That is why `She Sharp@ EY` resolves to `robotic-process-automation` — two names for one event on 5 March 2020 — which no amount of string matching would have found. A `match` of `hand-verified` means a person read the row; it does not mean the tag proves attendance. It does not. Humanitix is authoritative for who turned up; a tag records a list somebody pasted.
